## Course texts

Finch, W. H., Bolin, J. E., & Kelley, K. (2019). *Multilevel modeling using R* (2nd ed.). Chapman & Hall/CRC Press.

## Standard references

Gelman, A., & Hill, J. (2007). *Data analysis using regression and multilevel/hierarchical models*. Cambridge University Press.

Hox, J. J. (2010). *Multilevel analysis: Techniques and applications* (2nd ed.). Lawrence Erlbaum.

Raudenbush, S. W., & Bryk, A. S. (2002). *Hierarchical linear models: Applications and data analysis methods* (2nd ed.). Sage Publications.

Singer, J. D., & Willett, J. B. (2003). *Applied longitudinal data analysis: Modeling change and event occurrence*. Oxford University Press.

Snijders, T. A. B., & Bosker, R. J. (2011). *Multilevel analysis: An introduction to basic and advanced multilevel modeling* (2nd ed.). Sage Publications.

## Sources for the data used in this book

Leckie, G. (2013). *Cross-classified multilevel models*. LEMMA VLE Module 12. Centre for Multilevel Modelling, University of Bristol.

Raudenbush, S. W., & Bryk, A. S. (2002). High School and Beyond survey data. In *Hierarchical linear models*. Sage Publications.

Word, E. R., et al. (1990). *The State of Tennessee's Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) Project: Technical report 1985–1990*. Tennessee State Department of Education.

## On critical quantitative methods

Yosso, T. J. (2005). Whose culture has capital? A critical race theory discussion of community cultural wealth. *Race Ethnicity and Education, 8*(1), 69–91.
